applies_why: The judge text resolves a challenge where the challenger's pressed witnesses are cited as a footed chain, but it then relies on the pressed sentence's own words rather than weighing the two chains by footing.
quote: the challenger's covenant-origin analogy is footed (1 Chronicles 28:6, Acts 1:8) but the sentence's own words state the source of what is in the womb
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: "never verse by verse" and the retired stating-verse test: one reading forbids resolving a chain-press by citing the pressed sentence's own words; the other allows citing a verse's own words so long as no single contrary-stating verse is required. I read the rule as requiring chain-by-chain footing rather than verse-by-verse resolution.
why: The judge acknowledges the challenger's chain is footed, then decides by Matthew 1:20's own words instead of weighing the challenger's chain against the link's chain by footing.
